newsitem.title: UK: Copper, aluminium option vols soft, under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Copper, aluminium option vols soft, under pressure.

text.p: Copper and aluminium volatilities are under pressure as the underlying LME futures remain rangebound, prompting some players to liquidate long option positions, dealers said.
But nickel saw some robust buying on Thursday, taking advantage of weak volatility, they added.

Implied volatilities in copper and aluminium were about one to two points lower on the week, but had potential to slip further if the LME three months market continues its lacklustre performance, they added.
"I've heard of a couple market makers liquidating some positions. They're long of options, they've had enough of it, so they're getting out and starting again," one dealer said.
"You may see some more of that. They look good value here, but if people are liquidating positions, you think maybe they could go lower," he added.
Copper at-the-money (ATM) implied volatility was down about one point on the week, with May at around 13.00/16.00 percent and the rest of the year fairly flat from 14.00 to 16.50 percent.

Most market makers were long, being much more likely to opt for that side of the market since the Sumitomo crisis last year when many institutions with short positions suffered big losses when the market plummeted, traders said.
But now the market makers are losing money on their long positions since there is not enough volatility in the underlying futures to allow profitable hedging operations.
On the other hand, a Korean firm which is said to have granted large amounts of copper and aluminium strangles earlier in the year is doing quite well with its short position, traders added.

The market needs a jolt to attract more business, which could come from the Koreans buying back some options at lower levels, a breakout by futures, or a large operation by a bank who deemed volatilities were a good buy, traders said.

Aluminium implied ATM volatilities were also soft with quotes showing wide variations. May was quoted from bids as low as 11.00 percent up to 15.00 percent offers, June from 14.00 to 17.00 percent and fourth quarter at 14.50 to 16.00 percent.
Nickel has seen some buying over the past few days, traders said.
On Thursday alone, LME data shows total options volume in nickel was 815 lots, equivalent to 4,890 tonnes, all in call options.
Players were taking advantage of weaker vols after they fell a few weeks ago from levels above 30 percent for nearby dates early last month, traders said.
"It seems to be a volatility play. Vols are low, they are getting down to low historical levels and you can pick up upside calls for fairly cheap premiums," a trader said.
At-the-money fourth quarter material traded on Thursday at one point above the evening evaluation and $8,000 calls for the third quarter traded at 26 percent, dealers said.
They were also bid over 26 percent, but the market is thin and grantors stepped back, one said.
Zinc vols were a touch easier with June at 18.00 to 21.50 percent and July at 18.50 to 20.75 percent.
One trader said some selling had emerged on Thursday of some July $1,300 options at 19.75 and 20.00 percent.
Tin and lead were little moved in scant volume.
--London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
